label: Experience-machine joint models for the perfectionist, hedonist and mixed accounts
paraphrase: Finite controls on three lives (real, machine, drab) and four goods (achievement, friendship, knowledge, pleasure); real and machine share the rich profile, the machine life actually has only felt pleasure, the drab life only knowledge. PerfectIn is actual possession; betterness is strict respect dominance of the model's desirability (both transfer statements hold by construction) except in row 6. (1) Desirability as actual possession: the q.5 biconditional, q.5's perfect-in-act reading (trivially, since PerfectIn is Has), the case facts, the transfer statements and the stay-out verdict hold; experientialism fails. (2) Hedonist desirability (pleasure only, as presented): experientialism, the case facts and the transfer statements hold and the stay-out verdict fails; the backward half holds and the forward half fails; the real life dominates the drab life, whose profile differs. (3) Presentational experientialism (desirable in every presented good): experientialism and the forward half hold; the backward half, the biconditional and the stay-out verdict fail. (4) Partial experientialism (possession, plus friendship when presented): the forward half and the stay-out verdict hold; the backward half and experientialism fail. (5) Restricted (possession except knowledge): the backward half and the stay-out verdict hold; the forward half and experientialism fail. (6) With hedonist desirability and a betterness relating only real to machine, experientialism, same experience and the verdict hold and the transfer bridge fails. Statements about this finite interpretation only.
